abstract.t: RFC 3972 defines Cryptographically Generated Addresses (CGA), in which the Interface Identifier (IID) of an IPv6 address is derived from a cryptographic public key. The /64 subnet prefix is supplied by network infrastructure and has no cryptographic relationship to the key. This document specifies Hierarchical CGA (HCGA), an extension to RFC 3972 that also derives part of the upper 64 bits -- specifically the bits between the organizational prefix and the /64 boundary -- from the same public key. The result is an address whose full 128-bit value is a deterministic function of a public key (typically hardware-bound), an operator-controlled aggregate prefix, and two modifiers. HCGA is a traceability component intended for use within a larger accountability architecture that supplies key attestation, parameter distribution, and source-address enforcement; that architecture is not specified here. The capability supports workload network accountability in multi-tenant environments such as Kubernetes clusters, where infrastructure-assigned prefixes provide no per-instance cryptographic binding.
